papers.title: Single-Nucleus Multi-Omic Atlas Maps Regulatory Architecture and Non-Coding Variant Effects across Adult Human Tissues.
papers.abstract: Diverse human cell types establish specialized functions through lineage- and context-specific regulatory programs. Interpreting non-coding genetic risk requires integrated multi-omic reference maps that directly connect regulatory DNA to cellular expression across human tissues. Here we present a single-nucleus multiomic atlas comprising 459,856 transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility profiles from 21 adult human tissues across four donors, including paired measurements from 160,688 nuclei. We resolve nine cell lineages, 61 broad cell types and 313 subclusters, and identify 1,085,062 candi
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study presents a large-scale single-nucleus multi-omic atlas combining transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility profiles from 459,856 nuclei across 21 adult human tissues, including paired measurements from 160,688 nuclei. The atlas resolves nine lineages, 61 cell types, and 313 subclusters, and identifies over a million candidate regulatory elements, enabling interpretation of non-coding genetic variants in a tissue- and cell-type-specific context.

papers.title: Wastewater-based genomic surveillance uncovers broader SARS-CoV-2 diversity and spatial transmission dynamics in Georgia, January 2023-July 2024.
papers.abstract: Wastewater surveillance of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) using next-generation sequencing (NGS) enables real-time monitoring of circulating and emerging variants, often providing earlier detection than clinical reporting while capturing presymptomatic, asymptomatic, and symptomatic infections. However, the correlation between lineage abundance in wastewater and clinical specimens from corresponding sewersheds in Georgia remains understudied. From January 2023 through July 2024, the Georgia Public Health Laboratory (GPHL) sequenced SARS-CoV-2 from 669 wastewater s
papers.summary: This study used next-generation sequencing of wastewater samples across Georgia from January 2023 to July 2024 to track SARS-CoV-2 variants, finding that wastewater surveillance captured broader viral diversity and earlier detection of emerging lineages than clinical testing. The work also revealed spatial transmission dynamics across sewersheds, demonstrating the value of wastewater-based genomic surveillance as a complementary public health tool.

papers.title: Machine learning and computational approaches to model therapeutic response and resistance in diffuse midline glioma.
papers.abstract: Diffuse midline glioma (DMG) remains one of the most lethal cancers affecting children, adolescents and young adults and is near-universally resistant to treatment. Histone H3-alterations establish a profoundly dysregulated epigenetic landscape that promotes extensive intratumoral heterogeneity and cellular plasticity, key drivers of therapeutic resistance and treatment failure. Although single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics have transformed the study of tumor evolution, the mechanisms underpinning treatment resistance in DMG remain poorly understood. This Review examines how
papers.summary: This review discusses how machine learning and computational approaches are being applied to model therapeutic response and resistance in diffuse midline glioma (DMG), a lethal pediatric brain cancer driven by histone H3 mutations and epigenetic dysregulation. It highlights how single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics reveal intratumoral heterogeneity and cellular plasticity underlying treatment failure, and how computational models can integrate these data to predict drug response.

papers.title: DUET-seq: An Open-Source Droplet Platform for High-Fidelity Joint Chromatin and Transcriptome Profiling Reveals Temporal Regulatory Decoupling in Single Cells.
papers.abstract: Joint profiling of chromatin accessibility and gene expression in the same cell enables direct linkage of regulatory elements to transcriptional output, but existing approaches remain limited by low co-capture sensitivity, proprietary platforms, and high costs. Here we present DUET-seq, an open-source droplet microfluidic platform for joint profiling of chromatin accessibility and gene expression from the same nucleus. DUET-seq combines programmable dissolvable dual-linker hydrogel beads with one-step intra-droplet RT-PCR to physically co-index RNA and transposed chromatin fragments, completin
papers.summary: DUET-seq is an open-source droplet microfluidic platform that jointly profiles chromatin accessibility and gene expression from the same single nucleus, using dissolvable dual-linker hydrogel beads and one-step intra-droplet RT-PCR to co-index RNA and transposed chromatin fragments. The platform improves co-capture sensitivity over existing methods and reveals temporal decoupling between chromatin state and transcriptional output in single cells.

papers.title: Bridging BET bromodomain and immune checkpoint inhibitors through generative bioorganic frameworks for next-generation cancer immunotherapy.
papers.abstract: Bromodomain and extraterminal domain (BET) proteins are epigenetic readers that couple chromatin acetylation to oncogenic and immune-regulatory gene transcription, making them attractive targets for combination with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in precision oncology. This review synthesizes current mechanistic, medicinal-chemistry, and translational evidence on BET-ICI combination strategies. We describe how BET blockade reshapes tumor chromatin architecture, suppresses PD-L1 expression, and enhances antigen presentation, thereby increasing tumor susceptibility to immune-mediated attack
papers.summary: This review synthesizes mechanistic and medicinal-chemistry evidence on combining BET bromodomain inhibitors with immune checkpoint inhibitors for cancer therapy. It describes how BET blockade reshapes tumor chromatin architecture, suppresses PD-L1 expression, and enhances antigen presentation, increasing tumor susceptibility to immune attack. The authors also discuss generative bioorganic frameworks for designing next-generation combination agents.

papers.title: Machine Learning Guided Discovery of Microbiome Metabolites That Inhibit HDAC.
papers.abstract: Histone deacetylase (HDAC) is a family of key epigenetic regulator implicated in inflammation, metabolism, and cancer. Microbiome metabolites can modulate host histone acetylation, yet systematic identification of metabolites that target HDAC remains limited. Here we present a computationally driven discovery pipeline that combines training data composition optimization with experimental validation to prioritize microbiome-derived HDAC inhibitors. Starting from a large, public HDAC3 screening data set (314,129 compounds; 485 actives), we developed an automated iterative sampling strategy that
papers.summary: The authors built a machine learning pipeline to screen microbiome-derived metabolites for HDAC inhibition, using an iterative sampling strategy trained on a large public HDAC3 dataset (314,129 compounds). They prioritized candidate metabolites and validated them experimentally, demonstrating a computational route to discovering microbiome metabolites that modulate host epigenetics.

papers.title: Gravlax: an annotation-independent molecular evidence archive for single-cell RNA-seq.
papers.abstract: A cell-by-gene count matrix is the artifact of a single-cell RNA-seq experiment that is most often stored, shared, and reanalyzed. It is the output of a computation whose inputs are the sequenced molecules and a gene annotation, and while the molecules never change, the annotation is revised continually. Once the matrix has been produced, the evidence behind it can no longer be reinterpreted. Recovering that evidence means returning to raw reads or alignments that are large, costly to process, and frequently unavailable. We ask whether a concise representation of the molecules themselves can b
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Gravlax is a new data format that stores the molecular evidence from single-cell RNA-seq experiments independently of any gene annotation. This allows the same raw data to be re-annotated and reinterpreted as gene annotations are updated, without needing to reprocess large raw sequencing files. The tool addresses the problem that count matrices become obsolete when annotations change.

papers.title: Allele-Specific MicroRNA-Binding Variants at Colorectal Cancer Risk Loci in a Hispanic/Latino Population: An Integrative GWAS, All of Us, and Epigenomic Analysis.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) disproportionately affects Hispanic individuals, who remain underrepresented in genomic discovery and lack ancestry-matched functional resources. Many CRC risk variants are non-coding, and those in 3' untranslated regions (3' UTRs) can alter microRNA (miRNA) binding sites and reprogram post-transcriptional gene regulation. Here, we identify allele-specific miRNA-binding variants at CRC risk loci within the Hispanic population using a discovery pipeline anchored to Hispanic-relevant resources. CRC-associated 3' UTR variants were compiled from the GWAS Catalog, further ve
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This study identifies allele-specific microRNA-binding variants at colorectal cancer risk loci in a Hispanic/Latino population by integrating GWAS data, the All of Us cohort, and epigenomic annotations. The work addresses the underrepresentation of Hispanic individuals in genomic research and highlights how non-coding 3' UTR variants may alter post-transcriptional gene regulation relevant to CRC risk.

papers.title: SMORE: joint dimension reduction and cell population discovery on single-cell methylome data.
papers.abstract: Single-cell DNA methylation profiling technology captures novel epigenetic data modality but are challenging to analyze because of their heterogeneity, high dimensionality, and ultra-sparsity. Here we present SMORE (Single-cell MethylOme Reduction and Embedding), a computational method for joint dimensionality reduction and cell population discovery dedicated to single cell DNA methylation data. SMORE operates on a Bayesian framework that converts methylation proportions into ordered methylation states and jointly infers a low-dimensional representation, cell populations and their number. By u
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: SMORE is a new computational method for analyzing single-cell DNA methylation data, which is notoriously sparse and high-dimensional. It uses a Bayesian framework to simultaneously reduce dimensionality and discover cell populations (including their number) by converting methylation proportions into ordered methylation states. This provides a dedicated tool for a challenging emerging epigenetic data modality.

papers.title: HisTrader identifies nucleosome-free regions within ChIP-based profiling of histone post-translational modifications.
papers.abstract: Enhancers and promoters regulate cell identity through the binding of transcription factors (TFs) to specific DNA motifs within accessible chromatin. These regulatory regions are often identified using chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP)-based assays targeting histone modifications, such as ChIP sequencing (ChIP-seq), HiChIP, and proximity-ligation-assisted ChIP-seq (PLAC-seq). However, the large size of the enriched regions, or peaks, can make it difficult to pinpoint the precise DNA sequence where TFs act or where trait- or disease-associated variants exert their effects. We present HisTrad
papers.summary: HisTrader is a computational tool that identifies nucleosome-free regions (NFRs) from ChIP-based profiling of histone post-translational modifications, such as ChIP-seq, HiChIP, and PLAC-seq. By pinpointing these accessible regions within broad histone modification peaks, the method enables more precise localization of transcription factor binding sites and disease-associated variants. This improves the resolution of regulatory element mapping from widely used epigenomic assays.

papers.title: Using Brain Organoids to Explore Human Neurobiology.
papers.abstract: One of the major challenges in neuroscience is understanding how the human brain develops into a highly organized and functionally integrated organ, because many developmental processes cannot be investigated directly in humans and are not fully recapitulated in animal models. Brain organoids derived from human pluripotent stem cells have emerged as powerful three-dimensional (3D) experimental models that recapitulate key features of human neurodevelopment, including regional patterning, cellular diversification, and neural circuit assembly. Recent advances in long-term organoid culture, organ
papers.summary: This review discusses how brain organoids derived from human pluripotent stem cells serve as 3D models that recapitulate key features of human neurodevelopment, such as regional patterning and neural circuit assembly. It highlights recent advances in long-term culture that enable more faithful study of human brain biology where animal models fall short.

papers.title: Hybrid CNN and multi-head attention model for analyzing epigenetic mechanisms and gene expression across fungal phylogenetic distances.
papers.abstract: Understanding gene expression is crucial for optimizing biological processes in bioeconomic processes, human health, and environmental regulation. Epigenetic modifications significantly influence gene expression by altering chromatin structure and DNA accessibility. However, knowledge about the conservation of these mechanisms across species, especially in non-model organisms, is limited. This study predicts gene expression levels based on epigenetic modifications across fungal species, facilitating knowledge transfer from well-characterized to less understood species. We developed a deep lear
papers.summary: The authors developed a hybrid deep learning model combining convolutional neural networks and multi-head attention to predict gene expression levels from epigenetic modifications in fungi. The model enables knowledge transfer across fungal species with different phylogenetic distances, helping to infer expression in less-characterized non-model organisms. This work demonstrates the potential of deep learning to bridge gaps in epigenetic understanding across species.

papers.title: Multi-Omics Analysis and Experimental Validation Uncover Neddylation-Associated Biomarkers and Cellular Landscape in Lung Adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Accumulating evidence suggests that neddylation contributes to tumor initiation and progression. Nonetheless, its biological functions and regulatory mechanisms in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remain poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with experimental validation to characterize neddylation-related biomarkers and the cellular landscape in lung adenocarcinoma. The authors identify neddylation-associated molecular features that may serve as biomarkers and provide insights into how neddylation contributes to tumor biology in LUAD.

papers.title: "Updates on diagnostic and prognostic molecular biomarkers of CNS tumors".
papers.abstract: The diagnosis and classification of central nervous system (CNS) tumors has undergone a paradigm shift over the past decade, evolving from a purely histology-based approach to an integrated framework that incorporates molecular and epigenetic features. This review summarizes recent updates in key genomic and epigenomic biomarkers across major CNS tumor categories, with a focus on their diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic implications. DNA methylation profiling has emerged as a valuable tool for tumor classification, subgrouping, and grading, complementing traditional histopathologic assess
papers.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
papers.summary: This review summarizes recent advances in molecular and epigenetic biomarkers used to diagnose and classify central nervous system tumors, highlighting the shift from purely histology-based diagnosis to an integrated molecular framework. It emphasizes DNA methylation profiling as a key tool for tumor classification, subgrouping, and grading, alongside other genomic biomarkers with diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic relevance.

papers.title: Transcriptome-based epigenetic screening identifies DNA hypermethylation signatures as prognostic biomarkers in oral squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Promoter DNA hypermethylation is a key epigenetic mechanism of gene silencing in cancer, yet the DNA hypermethylome of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) and its prognostic relevance remain poorly characterized. Here, we systematically identified and validated novel hypermethylated genes with prognostic significance in OSCC using a genome-wide discovery and multi-platform validation strategy. Candidate genes were first identified by pharmacologic demethylation combined with RNA sequencing across OSCC cell lines, then validated by quantitative RT-PCR, methylation-specific PCR, and bisulfite se
papers.summary: This study systematically maps the DNA hypermethylome of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) by combining pharmacological demethylation with RNA sequencing across cell lines, then validating candidate hypermethylated genes using RT-PCR, methylation-specific PCR, and bisulfite sequencing. The authors identify DNA hypermethylation signatures that carry prognostic value, suggesting these epigenetic marks could serve as biomarkers for OSCC patient outcomes.

papers.title: The Epigenetic Aging-Cancer Continuum: Biomarkers, Metabolism, and Therapy.
papers.abstract: Aging and cancer form a biological continuum influenced by epigenomic changes, metabolic dysfunction, inflammation, cellular senescence, and loss of tissue homeostasis. Age-related epigenetic alterations can promote cancer, which exploits plasticity for evolution, immune evasion, metastasis, and resistance. Nutrition and metabolism affect this process through one-carbon metabolism, methyl-donor availability, acetyl-CoA and NAD+ balance, redox status, microbiome metabolites, and chromatin enzyme activity. Circulating biomarkers such as cell-free DNA methylation, mutation-based ctDNA, fragmentom
papers.summary: This review argues that aging and cancer exist on a biological continuum driven by epigenetic changes, metabolic dysfunction, inflammation, and cellular senescence. It highlights how nutrition and metabolism influence this process through one-carbon metabolism, methyl donors, acetyl-CoA and NAD+ balance, and microbiome metabolites, and discusses circulating biomarkers such as cell-free DNA methylation and ctDNA for tracking the continuum.

papers.title: Flow Orchestrated Regulatory Genomics Engine (FORGE): A Configurable Nextflow Pipeline for End-to-End snMultiome Analysis.
papers.abstract: Single-nucleus resolution multiome (snMultiome) assays concurrently profile gene expression and chromatin accessibility in the same nucleus. Yet regulatory inference from such analyses are difficult to scale, audit, and reproduce; moreover, as a field, snMultiomics and its' toolset remains far from standardized. To address these challenges we developed FORGE, a configureable Nextflow workflow that carries paired data from raw counts and fragments through regulatory network inference with a comprehensive differential testing suite. Execution is containerized, tracks provenance, robust to interr
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: FORGE is a configurable Nextflow pipeline that automates end-to-end analysis of single-nucleus multiome data, taking paired gene expression and chromatin accessibility counts from raw inputs through regulatory network inference and differential testing. It addresses the lack of standardization in snMultiome analysis by providing a containerized, provenance-tracking workflow that is reproducible and scalable.

papers.title: A comprehensive map of the bovine mobilome and their epigenetic regulation of mastitis.
papers.abstract: Retrotransposons are major components of mammalian genomes, yet their genome-wide annotation and epigenetic regulation in cattle remain incompletely characterized. Here, we present a comprehensive annotation and integrative epigenomic analysis of major retrotransposon classes in the bovine genome, with emphasis on DNA methylation patterns and their potential roles in subclinical mastitis. Using a multi-step de novo pipeline, we identified and classified long interspersed nuclear elements (LINEs), short interspersed nuclear elements (SINEs), and endogenous retroviruses (ERVs) in the bovine refe
papers.summary: This study provides a comprehensive genome-wide annotation of retrotransposons (LINEs, SINEs, and ERVs) in the bovine genome using a de novo pipeline, and integrates this with epigenomic data to examine DNA methylation patterns. The authors link retrotransposon methylation dynamics to subclinical mastitis, suggesting these mobile elements may play regulatory roles in the disease. It represents a new resource for understanding the bovine mobilome and its epigenetic regulation in the context of mastitis.

papers.title: The Exposome-Brain Axis: A Scoping Review of Biological Biomarkers in Environmental Neurotoxicity, Neuroinflammation, and Neurodegeneration.
papers.abstract: The escalating global burden of neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric disorders is deeply intertwined with cumulative environmental toxicant exposure. To accurately capture the prodromal and subclinical impacts of this multi-chemical "pollutome", research is shifting from symptom-based assessments toward the use of objective, quantifiable biological indicators. Guided by the PRISMA-ScR framework, this scoping review systematically analyzed literature across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase databases without temporal restrictions. The final selection included 52 human observational s
papers.summary: This scoping review synthesizes 52 human observational studies examining biological biomarkers that link environmental toxicant exposure (the 'exposome') to neurotoxicity, neuroinflammation, and neurodegeneration. It highlights a shift from symptom-based assessments toward objective, quantifiable biomarkers for capturing prodromal and subclinical neurological impacts of cumulative chemical exposures.

papers.title: H3K27me3 Drives Constricted Migration-Induced 3D Genome Rewiring in Melanoma.
papers.abstract: Repeated exposure of neoplastic cells to mechanical stresses during metastasis can drive stable morphological and physiological changes. We previously showed that A375 human melanoma cells subjected to 10 rounds of constricted migration ("Bottom-10 cells") became significantly more migratory and exhibited H3K9me3 relocalization, transcriptional remodeling, and chromatin compartment changes relative to naïve parental A375 cells. Because these phenotypes persist across cell divisions, we hypothesized they are driven and maintained by specific epigenetic mechanisms. We profiled candidate histone
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint investigates how repeated mechanical stress from constricted migration drives persistent epigenetic and 3D genome changes in melanoma cells. The authors find that H3K27me3 is a key driver of migration-induced genome rewiring, building on prior work showing H3K9me3 relocalization and chromatin compartment changes in repeatedly squeezed A375 cells. The study links mechanical forces during metastasis to stable epigenetic reprogramming.

papers.title: Sequencing the wastewater virome: Current strategies and bioinformatic pitfalls.
papers.abstract: Wastewater-based surveillance (WBS) is a powerful tool for monitoring viral pathogens at the population level, complementing clinical surveillance through anonymous and unbiased insights into viral circulation. Wastewater sequencing allows to move beyond detection toward detailed characterization of circulating pathogens. This review outlines the two main sequencing strategies used in WBS: targeted and untargeted approaches. Targeted methods, including amplicon- and probe-based sequencing, provide sensitive detection and recovery of known viruses but are limited in identifying novel pathogens.
papers.summary: This review examines sequencing strategies for wastewater-based surveillance of viral pathogens, contrasting targeted approaches (amplicon- and probe-based) that sensitively detect known viruses with untargeted methods capable of discovering novel pathogens. It also highlights common bioinformatic pitfalls in wastewater virome analysis, offering guidance for researchers designing population-level viral monitoring programs.

papers.title: Prioritization of candidate genomic regions for milking speed in Holstein cattle using international evaluations.
papers.abstract: Milking speed (MSPD) is an economically important trait in dairy cattle affecting labor efficiency, animal welfare and milking parlor productivity. This complex quantitative trait has been investigated to characterize its genetic basis and support genomic selection. Previous genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have reported genomic regions potentially related to MSPD; however, results vary considerably among studies and often provide limited functional interpretation. This study aimed to prioritize candidate genomic regions for MSPD based on the ranking of estimated SNP effects from the Int
papers.summary: This study prioritized candidate genomic regions associated with milking speed in Holstein cattle by ranking SNP effects from international genetic evaluations. The approach aims to refine inconsistent GWAS findings and provide better functional interpretation for genomic selection of this economically important trait.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Mass Spectrometry-Based Metabolomics and Lipidomics for Drug Discovery and Development.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence applied to mass spectrometry-based metabolomics and lipidomics has advanced through three technological generations: chemometric and classical machine learning, deep learning, and self-supervised foundation models, with large language models so far entering mainly at the edges. The metabolome and lipidome lie closest to drug action, yet they have been among the slowest omics layers to adopt modern artificial intelligence. This paradox arises from their downstream position, which leaves them without a closed molecular reference and without the standardized, readily model
papers.summary: This review traces how AI has been applied to mass spectrometry-based metabolomics and lipidomics across three generations: classical chemometrics/machine learning, deep learning, and self-supervised foundation models, with LLMs mostly at the periphery. It argues that despite being the omics layers closest to drug action, metabolomics and lipidomics have lagged in AI adoption due to their downstream position, lack of a closed molecular reference, and insufficient standardized data.

papers.title: VAEBAC: A representation-learning framework for proteome-scale prediction of amyloidogenic proteins and functional stratification of nucleic-acid-binding proteins.
papers.abstract: Nucleic-acid-binding proteins (NABPs) govern transcription, replication and genome organization, yet the distribution of aggregation susceptibility within regulatory proteomes remains unresolved. Here, we systematically examine amyloidogenic potential across the nucleic-acid-binding proteomes of four phylogenetically diverse organisms-Escherichia coli, Bacillus subtilis, Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Homo sapiens-spanning prokaryotes and eukaryotes, to determine whether aggregation-prone sequence architectures are selectively constrained within transcriptional networks.
papers.summary: The authors present VAEBAC, a representation-learning framework that predicts amyloidogenic (aggregation-prone) proteins at proteome scale and applies it to nucleic-acid-binding proteins across four organisms (E. coli, B. subtilis, S. cerevisiae, and human). The work examines whether aggregation-prone sequence features are selectively constrained within transcriptional regulatory networks, providing a functional stratification of NABPs.

papers.title: HINN prioritizes multi-omics biomarkers associated with cognitive decline.
papers.abstract: Integrating multi-omics data for disease prediction remains challenging due to the complexity of cross-layer biological interactions and the limited use of prior biological knowledge in many machine learning models. We present the Hierarchical Input Neural Network (HINN), a deep learning framework that incorporates biologically informed connections across genomic, epigenetic, and transcriptomic layers to model regulatory relationships in a structured and interpretable manner. HINN was applied to blood-derived multi-omics data to predict cognitive assessment scores, including MMSE, MoCA, ADAS11
papers.summary: The authors present HINN, a deep learning framework that uses biologically informed connections across genomic, epigenetic, and transcriptomic layers to predict cognitive assessment scores from blood-derived multi-omics data. The model is designed to be interpretable and to prioritize multi-omics biomarkers associated with cognitive decline.

papers.title: Metabolic modeling: the link between AI and multi-omics data to accelerate the discovery of antibiotic-resistant traits in ESKAPE pathogens.
papers.abstract: The development of predictive understanding of bacterial resistance to antibiotics is one of the greatest challenges of modern medicine. Genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) are mathematical representations of the metabolic network of a given organism assembled from genomic data that predict cellular activity across many environmental and genetic contexts. Because a single model can be solved under thousands of conditions, GEMs generate data at scales that support downstream analysis with artificial intelligence tools, helping to elucidate how pathogens adapt to host environments, evade immune
papers.summary: This review discusses how genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) of ESKAPE pathogens can be combined with AI and multi-omics data to predict antibiotic resistance traits. The authors argue that GEMs generate large-scale simulated data across many conditions, enabling machine learning to uncover mechanisms of host adaptation and immune evasion.

papers.title: Rapid Whole Genome Sequencing Enhances Pediatric Cancer Diagnosis.
papers.abstract: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) has been shown to improve diagnosis beyond standard-of-care genetic tests and guide precision treatment for childhood cancer. While WGS is now offered for children with suspected cancer in England, clinical workflows typically return results after several weeks whereas clinical decisions are often required within days. Here we evaluate feasibility and efficacy of a rapid WGS (rWGS) research workflow with streamlined bioinformatics to deliver clinical genomic findings (NCT07201038, Active, not recruiting). In 54 children with suspected or confirmed malignancy, rWGS
papers.summary: This study evaluates a rapid whole-genome sequencing (rWGS) workflow with streamlined bioinformatics for children with suspected or confirmed cancer, aiming to deliver clinical genomic findings within days rather than weeks. In 54 pediatric patients, the approach was assessed for feasibility and its ability to enhance diagnosis and guide precision treatment compared to standard-of-care genetic testing.

papers.title: Protocol for detecting germline copy number variants from whole-exome sequencing using agent-assisted Snakemake workflows.
papers.abstract: Germline copy number variants (gCNVs) are vital for diagnosing rare monogenic disorders. Here, we present a containerized, agent-assisted Snakemake protocol for detecting, annotating, and visualizing gCNVs from short-read whole-exome sequencing data. We describe steps for constructing baseline models, executing CNV calling, annotating variant pathogenicity using public datasets, and rendering interactive visual reports. This automated workflow simplifies routine management and ensures cross-platform reproducibility through a unified interface.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a containerized, agent-assisted Snakemake workflow for detecting, annotating, and visualizing germline copy number variants (gCNVs) from short-read whole-exome sequencing data. It covers baseline model construction, CNV calling, pathogenicity annotation using public datasets, and interactive visual reporting. The workflow aims to simplify routine management and ensure cross-platform reproducibility through a unified interface.

papers.title: Electronic Health Record-Based Phenotyping for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder: Algorithm Development and Multicenter Validation Study.
papers.abstract: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is a common psychiatric disorder, with two-thirds of affected individuals reporting severe impairment. Despite its substantial burden and moderate heritability, the etiology of OCD remains poorly understood, and treatments are often suboptimal. Although recent genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified some risk loci, much of the genetic architecture of OCD remains undiscovered, underscoring the need for scalable approaches to identify large, well-defined patient cohorts.
papers.summary: This study develops and validates an electronic health record-based phenotyping algorithm to identify obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) patients across multiple medical centers. The approach aims to enable scalable identification of large, well-defined OCD cohorts to support genetic and clinical research, given that much of OCD's genetic architecture remains undiscovered.

papers.title: Microbial community composition on polytetrafluoroethylene tape retrieved from implant screw channels: A cross-sectional high-throughput 16S rRNA sequencing study.
papers.abstract: To identify the types of microorganisms colonizing the surface of polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) tape used for sealing the central screw channel in implant prostheses and to evaluate their association with the duration of prosthetic functional loading.
papers.journal: Infection, genetics and evolution : journal of molecular epidemiology and evolutionary genetics in infectious diseases
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study used high-throughput 16S rRNA sequencing to characterize the microbial communities colonizing PTFE tape used to seal the central screw channel in implant prostheses, and examined whether community composition relates to how long the prosthesis had been in function. The work provides a culture-independent view of the bacteria that colonize this clinically relevant implant surface.

papers.title: Clinical Epigenomics in Rare Diseases: Interpreting DNA Methylation Episignatures.
papers.abstract: Epigenomic testing complements sequence-based analysis by detecting downstream changes in epigenomic state associated with genetic variation. Genome-wide DNA methylation episignatures are reproducible molecular phenotypes that can serve as biomarkers of specific Mendelian disorders, particularly those involving chromatin regulators, DNA methylation machinery, and transcriptional regulatory pathways.
papers.summary: This paper reviews how genome-wide DNA methylation episignatures can serve as reproducible biomarkers for rare Mendelian disorders, especially those caused by mutations in chromatin regulators and DNA methylation machinery. It argues that epigenomic testing complements standard sequence-based diagnostics by capturing downstream functional consequences of genetic variation.

papers.title: EndoPRS-SS: Summary-statistic based incorporation of endophenotypes to improve risk prediction.
papers.abstract: Endophenotypes are critical biological markers with genetic links to disease progression. We previously developed endoPRS, a multi-trait polygenic risk score (PRS) method that leverages endophenotype data to improve disease risk prediction. However, endoPRS requires individual-level genotype-phenotype data for model fitting, restricting its broader use. To address this, we introduce endoPRS-SS, an extension which enables PRS inference using genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics and LD reference panels. Through simulation and real data analysis, we demonstrate that endoPRS-SS
papers.summary: EndoPRS-SS extends the endoPRS multi-trait polygenic risk score method to work with GWAS summary statistics and LD reference panels instead of requiring individual-level genotype-phenotype data. This removes a key barrier to applying endophenotype-informed risk prediction, making it feasible for researchers who only have access to publicly available summary statistics. Simulations and real data analyses demonstrate its improved predictive performance.

papers.title: ArchMap is a web-based platform for reference-based analysis of single-cell datasets.
papers.abstract: Leveraging single-cell reference atlases to analyze new data has brought about a paradigm shift in single-cell data science akin to the first reference genome in genomics. However, methods for performing this mapping require computational expertise and, oftentimes, considerable compute power, limiting access for researchers who may benefit the most. Here ArchMap, a no-code query-to-reference mapping tool, removes this barrier by providing all-in-one automated mapping, cell-type annotation and collaborative features to analyze single-cell datasets from a wide range of integrated, often publishe
papers.summary: ArchMap is a no-code, web-based platform that lets researchers map new single-cell datasets onto existing reference atlases, automatically annotating cell types without requiring computational expertise or significant compute resources. It also includes collaborative features, aiming to democratize reference-based single-cell analysis for a broad range of researchers.

papers.title: Genome-Wide Identification and Structural Characterization of Secondary Metabolite Biosynthetic Gene Clusters in African Baobab (Adansonia digitata).
papers.abstract: Adansonia digitata L., known as the African Baobab, is renowned for its extraordinary longevity and its long-standing use in traditional African medicine. However, the genomic basis underlying its specialized secondary metabolism remains largely unexplored. This study aimed to computationally identify and characterize putative biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) within the publicly available A. digitata genome assembly (GenBank accession GCA_029448705.1) using an integrated bioinformatics pipeline. Ab initio gene structure prediction was performed with AUGUSTUS (Arabidopsis thaliana species mode
papers.summary: This study computationally scanned the publicly available African baobab genome to identify biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) responsible for secondary metabolite production, using an integrated bioinformatics pipeline with AUGUSTUS gene prediction. It provides a first genome-wide catalog and structural characterization of putative BGCs in this long-lived medicinal tree, laying groundwork for understanding its specialized metabolism.

papers.title: Analytical and clinical validation of the EdenDx methylation assay as a noninvasive supportive triage tool for early detection of endometrial cancer in cervical scraping specimens.
papers.abstract: Endometrial cancer (EC) is the most common gynecologic malignancy; however, early detection remains challenging due to overlapping symptoms and the absence of validated noninvasive triage testing. Diagnosis relies on invasive procedures such as endometrial biopsy or dilation and curettage. The EdenDx assay detects hypermethylation of CDO1 and CELF4 genes, which are specifically associated with EC and have been shown to be epigenetically altered prior to symptom onset. Here, we evaluate the clinical and analytical performance of the EdenDx assay as a noninvasive triage tool for the early detect
papers.summary: This study validates the EdenDx methylation assay, which detects hypermethylation of the CDO1 and CELF4 genes in cervical scraping specimens, as a noninvasive triage tool for early detection of endometrial cancer. The assay aims to reduce reliance on invasive procedures like endometrial biopsy or dilation and curettage by providing a supportive, noninvasive screening option.

papers.title: A Guide to Enzymatic Targeted Methylation Sequencing Bioinformatics Workflow: Best Practices.
papers.abstract: We present a best-practices protocol for targeted DNA methylation sequencing analysis that integrates both bisulfite- and enzymatic-conversion approaches using Twist Bioscience technology. Building on established tools and vendor-recommended workflows, this protocol provides a standardized, fully reproducible framework that addresses current gaps in the implementation, documentation, and downstream integration of targeted methylation sequencing analyses. The workflow incorporates widely used open-source tools across two main stages: preprocessing (adapter trimming with Trim Galore and quality
papers.summary: This protocol provides a standardized, reproducible bioinformatics workflow for analyzing targeted DNA methylation sequencing data generated with Twist Bioscience technology, covering both bisulfite and enzymatic conversion methods. It integrates widely used open-source tools for preprocessing (e.g., adapter trimming with Trim Galore) and downstream analysis, addressing gaps in implementation and documentation. The guide aims to help researchers consistently process and interpret targeted methylation data.

papers.title: Epigenetics in cancer: from mechanisms to precision medicine.
papers.abstract: Epigenetics encompasses heritable yet reversible changes in gene expression that occur without alterations to the underlying DNA sequence. Through coordinated regulation of DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin remodeling, and higher-order chromatin organization, epigenetic mechanisms shape chromatin accessibility and transcriptional programs that govern cellular identity, plasticity, and tissue homeostasis. In cancer, disruption of the epigenetic landscape has emerged as a hallmark of tumor initiation, progression, metastasis, immune evasion, and therapeutic resistance. Unlike gen
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how epigenetic mechanisms—DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin remodeling, and higher-order chromatin organization—are disrupted in cancer and contribute to tumor initiation, progression, metastasis, immune evasion, and therapy resistance. It argues that because epigenetic changes are reversible, they offer promising targets for precision medicine approaches in oncology.

papers.title: DeCTCF: Decoding CTCF binding sequences by leveraging predicted epigenomic features.
papers.abstract: CTCF is a key architectural protein with diverse roles in genome organization and gene regulation, yet how it achieves these roles in different contexts remains unclear. Pretrained sequence-based models such as Sei provide predicted epigenomic features that can be used in downstream analyses of regulatory elements. Here, we developed DeCTCF, an integrative computational framework that uses pretrained Sei predictions to analyze 236,552 CTCF binding sequences by integrating CTCF ChIP-seq data from 118 human cell lines. By leveraging predicted epigenomic features from the Sei model, we grouped th
papers.summary: DeCTCF is a computational framework that uses the pretrained Sei model's predicted epigenomic features to analyze 236,552 CTCF binding sequences across 118 human cell lines. By integrating these predictions with CTCF ChIP-seq data, it groups binding sites to reveal how CTCF achieves its diverse regulatory roles in different cellular contexts.

papers.title: Establishment of Uveal Melanoma Patient-Derived Organoids Using an Air-Liquid Interface System for Translational Research.
papers.abstract: Uveal melanoma (UM) is the most common primary intraocular malignancy in adults, with a unique genetic and epigenetic profile and a high metastatic risk. The lack of experimental models to replicate tumor biology, including its epigenetic landscape, limits progress in translational research. Recently, patient-derived organoid (PDO) models have emerged as a promising tool for the modeling of various tumors, including UM. This study aims to establish an air-liquid interface (ALI) PDO culture system for UM, evaluate its similarity to the primary tumors, and assess its utility for drug screening.
papers.summary: This study establishes patient-derived organoid models for uveal melanoma using an air-liquid interface culture system that better preserves the tumor's genetic and epigenetic features compared to traditional methods. The organoids closely resemble primary tumors and prove useful for drug screening, offering a new platform for translational research in this aggressive eye cancer.

papers.title: Deep Learning Predicts Hematopoietic Stem Cell Aging From 3D Chromatin Images.
papers.abstract: The functional decline of the hematopoietic system during aging affects organismal function and contributes to reduced healthspan. Quantifying hematopoietic aging holds great scientific and clinical relevance. Alterations in chromatin architecture are a well-established hallmark of aging that encode rich and informative signatures of the aging process, yet they remain largely unexplored as quantitative markers. Here, we present an interpretable deep learning approach based on convolutional neural networks, ChromAgeNet, that learns changes in the spatial features of chromatin architecture upon
papers.summary: The authors developed ChromAgeNet, a convolutional neural network that predicts hematopoietic stem cell aging from 3D chromatin images. By learning spatial features of chromatin architecture, the model provides an interpretable quantitative marker of aging. This demonstrates that chromatin organization encodes informative signatures of the aging process.

papers.title: Investigation of allele-specific expression in citrus hybrids reveals the association between siRNA-mediated de novo methylation and high expression in citrus genomes.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation plays a central role in the regulation of gene expression. In plants, methylation occurs in the CG, CHG, and CHH contexts, via distinct DNA methyltransferases including MET1, CMT3, and the RNA-directed DNA methylation (RdDM) pathway via DRM2. In interspecific hybrids, these epigenetic mechanisms are confronted to a mixed small RNA population and two subgenomes harbouring specific methylation patterns, therefore generating unique expression profiles. The aim of this work was to understand these regulations by analysing gene expression, DNA methylation, and small RNAs in a citrus
papers.summary: This study investigates allele-specific expression in citrus hybrids, examining how DNA methylation and small RNAs from two different subgenomes interact to regulate gene expression. The authors find that siRNA-mediated de novo methylation is associated with high gene expression in citrus genomes, revealing a unique epigenetic regulatory mechanism in interspecific hybrids.

papers.title: Spatial biology in cancer epigenetics.
papers.abstract: Cancer develops inside organized tissue environments wherein cellular behavior is heavily influenced by local interactions and spatially restricted regulatory programs. While bulk and single-cell sequencing technologies have fundamentally revolutionized our understanding of tumor biology, these techniques often disrupt tissue architecture and therefore fail to capture the spatial context in which molecular processes occur. Spatial transcriptomics has provided important insights into tumor heterogeneity, microenvironmental organization, and cell-to-cell communication. However, gene expression a
papers.summary: This review discusses how spatial biology approaches, particularly spatial transcriptomics, are being applied to cancer epigenetics to study how tumor cells and their microenvironment interact within intact tissue architecture. It highlights that while bulk and single-cell sequencing have advanced tumor biology, they lose spatial context, and spatial methods now offer new insights into tumor heterogeneity and cell-cell communication.

papers.title: A Pan-Methylome Framework for Population-Scale Bacterial Epigenomics.
papers.abstract: Epigenetic modifications furnish a hidden regulatory layer that shapes cellular fate and evolutionary potential without rewriting the genetic code. In eukaryotes, methylome maps have profoundly transformed our understanding of development, disease, and lineage diversification. In bacteria, which represent the most abundant and ecologically versatile forms of life, the epigenome remains a largely uncharted dimension. To enable population-scale comparison of bacterial methylomes, we develop a principled strategy to prioritize methylation systems that are enzymatically encoded, broadly conserved
papers.summary: The authors present a pan-methylome framework for systematically comparing bacterial DNA methylation systems across populations. By prioritizing methylation systems that are enzymatically encoded and broadly conserved, they enable population-scale epigenomic analysis in bacteria, a domain where methylome maps have lagged far behind eukaryotes. This provides a foundation for linking bacterial epigenetic variation to ecology and evolution.

papers.title: Single-cell DNA methylation profiling: Technologies, computation, and applications in precision oncology.
papers.abstract: Cancer is an intrinsically heterogeneous disease characterized by distinct malignant subclones defined by specific genetic and epigenetic alterations, such as aberrant DNA methylation. Traditional bulk sequencing methods analyze large populations of cells in aggregate, yielding an averaged methylome signal that masks the rare but clinically significant epigenetic patterns driving tumor initiation, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance. The emergence of single-cell DNA methylation (scDNAme) sequencing has driven a paradigm shift in oncology by providing the resolution required to dissect this
papers.summary: This review surveys single-cell DNA methylation (scDNAme) sequencing technologies, computational analysis methods, and their applications in precision oncology. It highlights how scDNAme overcomes the averaging effect of bulk sequencing to reveal rare epigenetic subclones driving tumor initiation, metastasis, and therapy resistance.

papers.title: Pan-cancer prognostic value of TGFBR1: Bioinformatics and experimental validation with a focus on gastric cancer.
papers.abstract: TGF-β receptor 1 (TGFBR1) is a key component of TGF-β signaling and has been implicated in tumor progression. However, its expression patterns, prognostic relevance and associated molecular contexts vary among malignancies and remain incompletely characterized within a consistent pan-cancer framework. In the present study, TGFBR1 expression, clinicopathological associations, survival outcomes, immune and stromal infiltration, genomic features, co-expression profiles and transcriptional programs were systematically evaluated using The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), TCGA-Genotype-Tissue Expression
papers.summary: This study systematically analyzed TGFBR1 expression across multiple cancer types using TCGA data, examining its associations with clinicopathological features, survival, immune/stromal infiltration, and genomic characteristics. The authors also performed experimental validation focused on gastric cancer, identifying TGFBR1 as a potential prognostic biomarker in this context.

papers.title: Epigenetic Insights in Pediatric Multiple Sclerosis: DNA Methylation Highlights an Involvement of Epstein-Barr Virus Infection and Host Immune Networks.
papers.abstract: Pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (PedMS) provides a unique opportunity to investigate MS pathogenesis because of the short interval between environmental exposures and disease onset. This study aimed to identify differentially methylated regions (DMRs) that mediate the interplay between environmental triggers and genomic factors in the early stages of the disease.
papers.summary: This study analyzed DNA methylation patterns in pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (PedMS) patients to identify differentially methylated regions linking environmental exposures to disease. The findings highlight involvement of Epstein-Barr virus infection and host immune networks, suggesting epigenetic mechanisms mediate the gene-environment interplay in early MS pathogenesis.

papers.title: Controlling for DNA dosage with whole-genome sequencing improves ATAC-seq peak calling.
papers.abstract: ATAC-seq is a powerful method for mapping chromatin accessibility and identifying cis-regulatory elements (CREs) across cell types. We reveal that ATAC-seq peak calling is compromised by local biases in DNA dosage, arising from copy number variations but also from DNA replication timing. As part of the FANTOM consortium's efforts, we propose enhancing the model-based analysis of ChIP-seq pipeline by integrating whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data, analogous to input controls in ChIP-seq analyses. This adjustment increases both the number and width of ATAC peaks, with improved proximity to trans
papers.summary: This paper shows that ATAC-seq peak calling is biased by local variation in DNA copy number and replication timing, which can create false or missed peaks. The authors propose incorporating whole-genome sequencing data as a control in the MACS pipeline, similar to input controls in ChIP-seq, which improves peak detection and better aligns peaks with regulatory regions.

papers.title: Whole-exome sequencing identifies a missense variant in the cytoskeletal gene SVIL implicating actin remodeling in COVID-19 severity in a Pakistani cohort.
papers.abstract: The current study investigated host genetic associations with disease severity in COVID-19 patients of South Asian origin and explored its molecular basis.
papers.summary: This study used whole-exome sequencing in a Pakistani cohort to identify host genetic variants associated with COVID-19 severity, finding a missense variant in the cytoskeletal gene SVIL. The finding suggests that actin remodeling pathways may influence how severely individuals respond to SARS-CoV-2 infection.

papers.title: VarSim: A Python Toolkit for HGVS Variant Description Validation, Normalization, and Representation Conversion.
papers.abstract: Accurate and reproducible representation of genetic variants is essential for clinical genomics, variant databases, and genomic research. The Human Genome Variation Society (HGVS) recommendations provide a standardized framework for describing sequence variants, but practical HGVS processing commonly involves multiple interdependent tasks, including parsing, validation, normalization, coordinate transformation, protein consequence inference, and conversion between variant representation formats. We developed VarSim, a lightweight Python toolkit that integrates these operations within a referen
papers.summary: VarSim is a lightweight Python toolkit that integrates parsing, validation, normalization, coordinate transformation, protein consequence inference, and format conversion for HGVS variant descriptions. It aims to streamline the often fragmented workflow of HGVS processing for clinical genomics, variant databases, and research applications.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence for precision gene therapy: emerging technologies, clinical applications, and future directions.
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is revolutionizing gene therapy from an empirical and iterative process to a predictive, data-driven and increasingly intelligent therapeutic development approach. This review covers the application of AI extensively throughout the gene therapy development process, from target therapeutic discovery, identification of disease genes, variant interpretation, integration of multi-omics data, optimization of CRISPR, engineering of the vector, prediction of immunogenicity, manufacturing, and clinical development and post-marketing surveillance. The role of machine learni
papers.summary: This review surveys how artificial intelligence is being applied across the entire gene therapy pipeline, from identifying disease genes and interpreting variants to optimizing CRISPR design, engineering vectors, predicting immunogenicity, and supporting manufacturing and post-market surveillance. It highlights the shift from empirical, iterative gene therapy development toward predictive, data-driven approaches and outlines emerging technologies and future directions.

papers.title: The complete mitochondrial genome of Zamia integrifolia uncovers distinct patterns of genomic turnover and repeat expansion in Zamiaceae.
papers.abstract: Gymnosperm mitochondrial genomes exhibit substantial variation in size and structure, yet the evolutionary dynamics of Cycadales remain insufficiently explored beyond the genus Cycas.
papers.summary: This study reports the complete mitochondrial genome of the cycad Zamia integrifolia, providing the first detailed mitogenome characterization for the genus Zamia. Comparative analyses reveal distinct patterns of genomic turnover and repeat expansion within Zamiaceae, highlighting structural variation in gymnosperm mitochondrial genomes.

papers.title: Precision engineering of upstream open reading frames for translational regulation and crop improvement.
papers.abstract: Upstream open reading frames (uORFs) are pervasive cis-regulatory elements in the 5'untranslated regions (UTRs) of eukaryotic mRNAs that modulate translation of downstream main open reading frames (mORFs) by shaping ribosome scanning, initiation, and reinitiation. By operating downstream of transcription, uORFs enable fine-scale control of protein abundance, offering a distinctive regulatory layer for precise tuning of gene expression in plants. Recent advances in ribosome profiling, translation initiation-site mapping, peptidomics, computational annotation, and genome editing have expanded th
papers.summary: This review discusses how upstream open reading frames (uORFs) in the 5' untranslated regions of plant mRNAs act as cis-regulatory elements that fine-tune translation of downstream main genes. It highlights recent advances in ribosome profiling, translation initiation-site mapping, and genome editing that enable precise engineering of uORFs for translational regulation and crop improvement.

papers.title: A machine learning framework for interpreting phylogenetic tree patterns in interkingdom horizontal gene transfer.
papers.abstract: Horizontal gene transfer (HGT), the movement of genetic material between unrelated organisms, is widely recognized as an important driver of genome evolution in bacteria. In eukaryotes, however, the evolutionary impact of HGT remains debated. The identification of interkingdom HGT (iHGT) is especially challenging due to the lack of gold standard methods. While automated approaches for iHGT candidate detection exist, the interpretation of phylogenetic tree topologies into biologically meaningful evolutionary patterns has traditionally depended on expert manual inspection, a process that is subj
papers.summary: This paper presents a machine learning framework designed to automatically interpret phylogenetic tree topologies for detecting interkingdom horizontal gene transfer (iHGT), replacing the traditionally manual expert inspection process. The approach aims to standardize and scale the identification of HGT events between bacteria and eukaryotes, where gold-standard methods are lacking.

papers.title: ChoCallate: a computational pipeline for consensus germline variant calling in genomic sequencing data.
papers.abstract: Accurate germline variant calling in non-model and polyploid organisms remains challenging due to sequencing errors, genomic complexity, and caller-specific biases. Existing ensemble methods of variant calling are constrained by species-specific training, limited portability, or an inability to process multiple samples concurrently. To address these limitations we developed ChoCallate, a Nextflow-based pipeline for consensus germline variant calling. The pipeline integrates three species-independent callers, bcftools, FreeBayes, and Genome Analysis Toolkit (GATK) HaplotypeCaller, within a flex
papers.summary: ChoCallate is a Nextflow-based pipeline that combines three species-independent variant callers (bcftools, FreeBayes, and GATK HaplotypeCaller) to produce consensus germline variant calls. It is designed to handle non-model and polyploid organisms, addressing limitations of existing ensemble methods such as species-specific training and inability to process multiple samples concurrently.

papers.title: The causal integration ladder: a multilevel evidence framework for therapeutic target evaluation in cervical cancer.
papers.abstract: Cervical-cancer genomic studies nominate many altered genes, but the evidence needed to distinguish disease association from a causal, therapeutically tractable mechanism is rarely stated explicitly. We present the Causal Integration Ladder (CIL), an evidence-accounting framework that distinguishes Level I association, inherited Level II-G evidence, acquired Level II-S evidence, Level III computational and direct functional evidence, and Level IV translational validation, while treating viral etiology as an explicit context modifier. An exploratory TCGA-CESC screen (306 tumours, 3 normal sampl
papers.summary: The authors propose the Causal Integration Ladder (CIL), a structured framework for grading evidence that links genomic alterations in cervical cancer to causal, therapeutically actionable mechanisms, distinguishing association from inherited, acquired, functional, and translational evidence while accounting for viral etiology. They apply it in an exploratory TCGA-CESC screen of 306 tumors to demonstrate how the framework organizes target evaluation.

papers.title: Novel Strategy for Structural Variant Genotyping by Short-Read Genomic Sequencing From Restriction-Circles: Experimental and Bioinformatics Proof-of-Concept.
papers.abstract: Structural variants (SVs) comprise copy-number variants (e.g., deletions and duplications) and copy-neutral SV (e.g., perfect inversions). Short-read high-throughput DNA-sequencing is the established technology for small-variant calling in clinical genomics, whereas Oxford nanopore or PacBio long-read NGS technologies improve SV identification but remain challenging to implement in clinical settings. We developed and validated a novel experimental protocol and bioinformatics pipeline for SV genotyping from short-read whole-genome sequencing (WGS) of restriction-circles of DNA. The experimental
papers.summary: The authors developed a new experimental protocol and bioinformatics pipeline that uses restriction enzyme digestion to create circular DNA molecules, enabling short-read whole-genome sequencing to genotype structural variants (including inversions and copy-number changes) that normally require long-read technologies. This proof-of-concept demonstrates that short-read sequencing of restriction-circles can detect SVs, potentially making SV genotyping more accessible in clinical settings.

papers.title: TattleTail: A Rule-Based Tool for Identifying Canonical Pyocin-Encoding Gene Clusters in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
papers.abstract: Tailocins are phage tail-like bacteriocins derived from prophages that have lost the ability to package viral genomes while retaining bactericidal activity against related bacterial strains. In Pseudomonas aeruginosa, these elements are referred to as pyocins and contribute to ecological fitness and antimicrobial applications. Despite lacking essential phage components, pyocin-encoding gene clusters share substantial sequence homology with phage tail genes, creating a major challenge for genome annotation. Current prophage prediction tools, which rely on phage gene homology, can frequently mis
papers.summary: TattleTail is a rule-based bioinformatics tool designed to identify canonical pyocin-encoding gene clusters in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, which are phage tail-like bacteriocins that are difficult to distinguish from prophages due to shared sequence homology. The tool addresses the limitations of existing prophage prediction methods that frequently misannotate these clusters, providing a more accurate approach for genome annotation of these antimicrobial and ecologically important elements.

papers.title: Knowledge Mapping of Human Genetic Variation in Multiomics Biomarker Translation: A Bibliometric Analysis.
papers.abstract: Human genetic variation and multiomics biomarker translation has emerged as a rapidly developing research field at the intersection of molecular medicine, bioinformatics, and clinical decision-making. This study used bibliometric methods to map its global structure, intellectual base, and thematic evolution. The eligibility framework was deliberately restricted to studies in which inherited or somatic human genetic variation was substantively linked to omics-integrated biomarker discovery, functional interpretation, clinical stratification, or therapeutic response; generic omics studies withou
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis maps the research landscape at the intersection of human genetic variation and multiomics biomarker translation, identifying key intellectual structures, thematic trends, and collaborative networks. It provides a global overview of how inherited and somatic variation is being linked to omics-integrated biomarker discovery and clinical stratification. The study is descriptive rather than experimental, offering guidance for researchers and funders on the field's evolution.
